summary: The 24-episode Gonzo anime adapts manga Acts (chapters) 1-30 only partially and out of a straight line: Wikipedia's episode-list lead states the first three volumes are adapted across the first thirteen episodes with the remainder 'primarily an original story line that occasionally still pulls from the source manga', and MangaUpdates states the anime starts Vol 1 Ch 1 and 'Ends at Vol 5, Chap 30 (Skips Chap 7, 12-18) Diverges to an original ending'. Faithful front: eps 1-4 = Acts 1-6 (v1, incl. the Azmaria casino arc, her debut ch 3 = ep 3 per fandom infobox), eps 9-10 = the v2 flashback (Acts 8-11), ep 13 = the Marionette Train arc (Acts 19-21, end of v3). Eps 5-8 and 11-12 are anime-original bridge stories (their chapter-number span, Acts 7 and 12-18 — including Satella's manga intro arc 15-17 — is on MU's skip list; Satella instead debuts via an original mission in ep 6). Eps 14-21 loosely/divergently parallel v4-v5 (Pursuers alliance, carnival battle eps 18-20 ~ Acts 27-30; ep 16's antagonist Eliza Brown is anime-exclusive; ep 21 grafts the v6 Mary Magdalene flashback, her manga debut ch 36), and eps 22-24 are the famous anime-original ending. The stored ep24→ch30 anchor is MU's series-level bound misplaced on the finale; the bound belongs at ep 20 and the finale adapts nothing.

anchors.note: Ep title 'Sister Rosette' = Act 1 'Her name is Sister Rosette'; same intro mission (restaurant demon, building destroyed); MU: anime starts Vol 1 Chap 1
Ep title 'Contractor' = Act 2 'Chrono's Contract'; contract/timepiece unsealing reveal in both; Joshua nightmare cameo is a graft (his manga debut is ch 9)
Azmaria arc begins: her fandom infobox debut = anime ep 3 / manga ch 3; casino/escape half of Acts 3-6; internal 3/4 vs 5/6 split across eps 3-4 is inferred from arc structure
Azmaria arc/volume 1 boundary: blimp rescue + apostle awakening = Acts 5-6 ('Angel on the Altar', 'The Cry to Awaken'); Act 7 is on MU's skip list so adapted v1 content ends at 6

Seventh Bell flashback begins: Rosette/Joshua childhood, tomb of Mary Magdalene, meeting Chrono = v2 flashback opening (Joshua manga debut ch 9 per fandom); MU skip list omits 8-11 i.e. they ARE adapted
Flashback conclusion: Aion gives Chrono's horns to Joshua, orphanage frozen/stone = v2 core (Goodreads v2 blurb matches beat-for-beat); Acts 12-14 of v2 skipped per MU

Marionette Train arc (Acts 19-21 'Marionette Train 1-3', end of v3): Rizelle's train attack/death matches manga per fandom Rizelle page + tropedia (ep 13 web attack); Wikipedia lead: first three volumes across first thirteen episodes

Carnival evening = Acts 27-28 ('Night of the Carnival', 'Under the Starry Sky', v4 end); battle erupts ep 19 which tropedia places 'about midway through the 5th volume'; whole stretch is a divergent retelling, see annotation

MU's declared adaptation bound: 'Ends at Vol 5, Chap 30'; the carnival/atonement battle climax parallels Acts 29-30, but key beats (Chrono ripping Joshua's horns, Chrono turned to stone, Joshua's mind breaking) are anime-only per ja.wikipedia

continue_points.note: Honest resume is a restart: WDTALO says you 'technically cannot' continue where the anime ends and recommends reading from the beginning (minimum: v8, chs 49-56, for the true ending). Mechanical bound would be ch 31 (MU bound ch 30), but Acts 7 and 12-18 were never adapted and eps 14-24 are divergent, so ch 31 misleads.

annotations.note: Satella (manga debut Act 15 'The Witch of New York', v3, per fandom infobox) is introduced via an anime-original mission; her manga intro arc Acts 15-17 sits inside MU's skipped range and is never directly adapted
Rizelle's 'Puppetmaster' Grand Central attack is an anime-original story borrowing the spider/puppet concept from the Marionette Train arc, which is then adapted properly in ep 13

Pursuers alliance vs Sinners loosely parallels early v4 (Duffau exists in the manga) but is primarily anime-original per Wikipedia's lead; ep 16's antagonist Eliza Brown is anime-exclusive per her fandom page

Carnival battle / ritual of atonement retold divergently: tropedia places the ep-19 battle ~mid-v5, MU bounds the adaptation at ch 30, and ja.wikipedia details anime-only outcomes (Joshua's horns ripped off, Chrono time-frozen/stone, Joshua's mental collapse)
Mary Magdalene/Aion 'Magdalene' flashback pulls v6 material out of order (her manga debut is ch 36 per fandom infobox; manga tells it much later and differently); do not treat as a forward anchor

Famous anime-original ending (Rosette saint-ification, Satella/Fiore mutual death in a barrier, Aion survives — all anime-only per ja.wikipedia); manga chs 31-56 (and the real ending, v8) were never adapted

type_corrections.note: Anime-original bridge stories with canon cast/continuity (militia test, Seal of Seven Wings/early Aion, Rizelle at Grand Central, Gabriel Hound, Christmas): their chapter-number span (Acts 7, 12-18) is explicitly on MU's skip list, and Wikipedia's lead fits only vols 1-3 into eps 1-13, leaving these episodes without manga counterparts. Without correction, eps 11-12 would interpolate into the skipped Acts 13-18.

Wikipedia lead: from ep 14 the series is 'primarily an original story line that occasionally still pulls from the source manga'; ep 16's plot centers on anime-exclusive Eliza Brown (fandom: appearances = Anime only, 'only appearing in an anime-exclusive... Episode 16')
Divergent retellings of manga material (Acts 27-30 carnival battle; ch 36+ flashback in ep 21) interwoven with anime-only outcomes detailed on ja.wikipedia
Anime-original ending, no manga counterpart (manga's ending differs in events and tone; Aion survives only in the anime)

repairs.why: The stored ep24→ch30 v5 anchor is MangaUpdates' SERIES-level statement ('Ends at Vol 5, Chap 30... Diverges to an original ending') misplaced onto the finale. The finale itself is anime-original (Wikipedia lead; WDTALO: you 'technically cannot' continue from it; ja.wikipedia details the anime-only ending) and adapts no chapter — finales anchor to what they adapt. The ch-30 bound belongs at ep 20 (new anchor supplied), and ep 24 should carry no chapter anchor, only the divergence annotation + continue point.

structure.notes: Single 24-episode season (AniList 60), no OVAs/movies. Chapter space = manga 'Act' numbers 1-56 mainline (MU/fandom/Wikipedia all agree); context total_chapters=59 evidently counts the two Extras ('Doll in the Skyscraper' after Act 21 v3; 'Elizabeth, 1921' after Act 48 v7) and the v8 Epilogue — anchors here use Act numbers only. Volume boundaries (Wikipedia + fandom manga page): v1=1-6, v2=7-14, v3=15-21, v4=22-28, v5=29-35, v6=36-42, v7=43-48, v8=49-56. Adaptation shape: Acts 1-6 (eps 1-4), Acts 8-11 (eps 9-10), Acts 19-21 (ep 13) faithful-ish; Acts 7 and 12-18 skipped entirely (MU); Acts 22-30 loosely/divergently paralleled in eps 14-20; ch 36-41 flashback grafted into ep 21; eps 22-24 original ending; Acts 31-35 and 42-56 never adapted.

flags_for_sean: ep24 anchor repair proposes REMOVAL (new=null) with the ch-30 bound relocated to ep 20 — apply script must support anchor deletion or treat as move.

Apparent conflict resolved, for the record: fandom infoboxes give Satella 'debut anime ep 6 / manga ch 15' while MU says chs 12-18 were skipped — debut fields mark first appearances in each medium, not that ep 6 adapts ch 15; ep 6 is an original intro (graft annotation).
ep 2 anchor rests on title correspondence (Contractor / Chrono's Contract) + contract-reveal beat; no source states 'ep 2 = Act 2' verbatim — marked medium.

continue_from_chapter set to 1 (WDTALO full-restart recommendation) rather than mechanical 31; if the schema wants a forward-only value, 31 is the alternative but understates the divergence (Acts 7, 12-18 also never adapted).
Sub-splits inside two-episode arcs (ep3=3-4/ep4=5-6, ep9=8-9/ep10=10-11) are structural inferences within multi-source-confirmed arc spans; arc END boundaries (6, 11, 21) are the load-bearing values.
